messages:
Sam (AE): Hi team — Luca's cloud security lead asked a few POC questions we need answers for before next week's demo: can we guarantee EU-only data residency for inference, which subprocessors are involved in EU regions, and what happens if EU capacity is exhausted? Also customer asked rough pricing delta between Hosted EU endpoints vs a small Dedicated pool.
Jo (SE): short answers up front: yes for EU-only (with caveats), subprocessors list in our docs, and fallback behavior is configurable (default is cross-region fallback unless you lock routing).
Jo (SE): details: Hosted EU endpoints run in our eu-west-1 / eu-central-1 regions. By default we route by latency to the nearest healthy region; we have a routing policy flag you can set on the tenant: `region_preference: eu` or `region_strict: true` to prevent cross-region fallback.
Jo (SE): example config for the POC:
```
routing_policy:
  mode: region_strict
  allowed_regions: [eu-west-1, eu-central-1]
  fallback: none
```
Jo (SE): with `region_strict` requests will 403 if no EU capacity, so SLA risk is on the customer/POC but guarantees no egress to non-EU.
Sam (AE): Luca — does your security team need auto-failover blocked entirely or are they ok with a manual fallthrough to our US region if we notify them?
Luca (Customer): They want no data leaving EU for now. Manual failover okay but must be in writing. Also want names of subprocessors (hosting, monitoring, telemetry).
Priya (Security): We can produce the DPA + the EU subprocessors list. Currently EU infra is hosted on GCP eu-west/central; subprocessors: `GCP (compute)`, `Datadog (optional metrics ingestion)`, `Sentry (error traces, opt-in)`, `Cloudflare (edge)`, `AWS KMS partner` for customer-managed keys in some installs. Full list and contracted locations: https://redwood.example.com/subprocessors (internal link).
Priya (Security): For the POC we'll propose: disable optional telemetry, enable tenant-level KMS (if customer wants keys in EU KMS), and set `region_strict` so nothing leaves EU. We'll also provide a scoped SOC2 + pen-test summary and support adding a contractual subprocessor clause.
Jo (SE): on Dedicated vs Hosted pricing — ballpark: Hosted EU (pay-as-you-go) is per-token plus small infra surcharge for dedicated region: ~ $0.XX/token (depends on model). Small Dedicated pool (reserved) has monthly commit (e.g., €Xk/month) but unit cost goes down significantly at scale and gives capacity isolation and zero cross-region fallback. I'll DM exact ranges to Sam for the quote.
Sam (AE): Action items: 1) Jo to prepare POC config + runbook for `region_strict` and telemetry off. 2) Priya to attach DPA + subprocessor list + KMS options. 3) Jo to include latency SLO numbers for eu-west-1 vs eu-central-1 and recommended GPU sizes for low-latency POC. 4) Sam to update customer with action plan and dates.
infra-bot: Ticket RED-POC-137 created for 'EU-only POC: routing & subprocessors' assigned to Jo and Priya.
Jo (SE): latency notes for POC: typical single-request p95 token latency in eu-west-1 for small model ~ 120-180ms, for medium model 250-400ms. If you need <100ms we should size Dedicated with NVLink GPU family and tune batching.
Luca (Customer): Got it. Can we schedule the POC for next Tues? also need an estimate for the time to stand up a small Dedicated pool if we go that route.
Jo (SE): if Dedicated: provisioning ≈ 5-7 business days (procurement + capacity). For a fast POC we can run Hosted with `region_strict` and dedicated configs to mimic committed behavior.
Priya (Security): one more: provide retention config for logs and audit trails. We'll set default to 30 days for POC and offer 90/365 options for enterprise.
Sam (AE): Perfect — I'll confirm next Tues and transfer the quote to procurement. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Luca (Customer): Thanks everyone, appreciate the quick answers.
Sam (AE): I'll post the POC runbook link once Jo shares it.
Jo (SE): uploading runbook to the thread — https://redwood.example.com/internal/pocs/eu-region-strict-runbook (will share perms).
